name: Joash
overview: Joash was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, uniquely identified as the son of Becher. His mention in Scripture is brief and focused on his genealogical placement within the tribe. No additional notes provide further detail about his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Joash means 'YHWH has bestowed,' reflecting a recognition of God's gift or blessing. This proper name is not indicated as given directly by God, but it carries a meaningful theophoric element that honors the Lord.
familyAndRelationships: Joash is explicitly recorded as the son of Becher, situating him within the Benjaminite lineage. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not record any other family connections for him.
scriptureSignificance: Joash's significance lies primarily in his genealogical identity as a descendant of Benjamin through Becher. His inclusion in the biblical record helps preserve the lineage and tribal heritage important for understanding Israel’s family structures. Although not noted for specific actions or events, his mention supports the broader biblical narrative of God's providential care in maintaining His people’s genealogies.
